paragraphs.text: Congenital prothrombin (factor II) deficiency is among the rarest inherited coagulation disorders (Lancellotti and De Cristofaro, 2009). Two main phenotypes are distinguished: hypoprothrombinemia (type I deficiency), with concomitantly low levels of prothrombin activity and antigen, and dysprothrombinemia (type II deficiency), with normal or near-normal synthesis of a dysfunctional protein; compound heterozygosity for hypoprothrombinemia and dysprothrombinemia has also been described (Lancellotti and De Cristofaro, 2009). Low prothrombin activity typically prolongs both the activated partial thromboplastin time and the prothrombin time, and clinical manifestations are predominantly mucosal or surgical- or trauma-associated bleeding, although joint bleeding and intracranial hemorrhage have been reported (Meeks and Abshire, 2008).

agent.process_note: Read every file in full: 23 abstracts and 12 title-only records. No full texts were available. The title-only papers have no content beyond their titles. I cited only a few of them, for variant names in Nomenclature, and drew no clinical details from them. The causal gene (prothrombin, F2) and the inheritance pattern come from Poort 1994 (homozygous Y44C with cosegregation), Akhavan 2000 (homozygous and compound heterozygous patients; autosomal recessive), and the compound heterozygotes reported by Iwahana 1992, Morishita 1992 and Lefkowitz 2000. No reference data were supplied, so the intro gives no gene MIM number; the chromosome 11 location comes from two review abstracts. I did not list Akhavan 2000's nine mutations as separate allelic variants, because the abstract does not say which patient carried which mutation or with what zygosity; its kringle-1 change is kept as printed ('Asp118Try'). Segal 2009 (G20210A thrombophilia) and Lanchantin 1968 (amino acid composition) do not concern this disorder and were not cited. Heterozygous dysprothrombinemia with mild bleeding (Lutze 1989) and the 'autosomal dominant' asymptomatic Mexico City variant are described in the text but not coded as AD inheritance.
